Users can now create fully licensed music, voiceovers, and sound effects on Adobe's Firefly AI assistant. Here are the details.

Firefly audio tools officially launch

Adobe recently partnered with Berklee College of Music (Berklee College of Music) to conduct a survey to understand the workflows and challenges of video creators, musicians, and marketers. According to Adobe, all respondents said they use music in videos, with 32.7% using AI-generated music. 43.2% of respondents identified legal and copyright risks as the main barrier to using music, while 38.9% cited licensing fees.

Today, Adobe officially launches the Generate Music tool on Firefly, along with two other tools: Generate Speech and Generate Sound Effects:

Generate Music can create original, fully licensed tracks that match the length and mood of your video, allowing your music to be used anywhere with your content without worrying about licensing or takedown issues. Generate Speech can convert scripts into clear, natural-sounding voiceovers, with the option to use Adobe's own Firefly voice model or ElevenLabs. Generate Sound Effects can create custom sound effects that match the actions, rhythm, and energy of your content.

Adobe emphasizes that the music created by Generate Music is fully licensed and ready for immediate use in final products, just like Generate Speech and Generate Sound Effects, with no additional subscription required to generate commercially usable assets.

Generate Music can analyze video content and create editable prompts based on the most suitable soundtrack it identifies. Users can also adjust parameters such as tempo, energy, and duration, then press Generate to receive four options.

When using Generate Speech, users can add emotional expression and pronunciation markings to certain parts of the script; Generate Sound Effects allows users to input text prompts or record sounds with their own voice as a reference for generating audio.

Below is Adobe's explanation:

The new tools are now available on Adobe Firefly's desktop and mobile web applications.

Adobe expands AI model lineup in Firefly

Additionally, Adobe announced today that Gemini Omni Flash has landed on Firefly, allowing users to "prompt with video, audio, and images combined with text input, giving you more ways to develop videos and reshape them through iterative edits…".

This follows Adobe's recent addition of Runway Aleph 2.0 and Kling 2.0 to its third-party model toolkit, which previously included models from Google, Kling AI, Luma AI, OpenAI, Runway, and Adobe itself.
